articles.headline: Middle Tennessee vs. FIU live stream, where to watch online, CBS Sports Network finder, odds
keyFacts: CBS Sports Network will broadcast six college football games during Week 8, beginning with Middle Tennessee at FIU on Tuesday.
The schedule includes a triple-header on Saturday featuring matchups between Western Michigan and Toledo, North Texas and Navy, and Utah State and Texas State.
Viewers can watch all six games on the CBS Sports Network or stream them through the CBS Sports website and mobile app.
body: The college football season officially enters its second half in Week 8, and CBS Sports Network will carry six games to kick off the back half of the schedule, starting on Tuesday and rolling all the way through a triple-header on Saturday.

The action starts on Tuesday night at 7 p.m. ET with a Conference USA clash, as Middle Tennessee travels to Miami to take on FIU in a battle of 3-3 squads. On Thursday at 7 p.m., Liberty heads south to Kennesaw State as a road favorite as the Flames look to remain unbeaten in conference play. The weeknight slate closes with a Friday night battle in the northeast as UMass goes on the road to take on UConn at 7 p.m.

Saturday's triple-header begins in Toledo at 12 p.m., where the Rockets host Western Michigan in a matchup of two of the MAC's best in the Glass Bowl. That'll be followed by North Texas flying out to Annapolis to take on Navy at 3:30 p.m., with the Mean Green hoping to remain undefeated in conference and keep their dreams of another trip to the conference title game alive. Finally, Utah State will head to San Marcos to face Texas State in a Pac-12 showdown at 7:30 p.m., with the Bobcats fresh off a dominant offensive performance a week ago.
CBS Sports Network will carry all six games, with full viewing info, betting lines and key storylines to follow as Week 8 unfolds.
All times Eastern | Odds via SportsLine consensus
Middle Tennessee vs. FIU
Date: Tuesday, Oct. 20 | Time: 7 p.m.
Location: South Dade Kia Field at Pitbull Stadium -- Miami, Florida
TV: CBS Sports Network [Channel finder]
Live stream: CBSSports.com | Mobile: CBS Sports App
Spread: FIU -10

The Panthers are strong favorites at home despite sharing the same record (both overall and in conference) as the Blue Raiders. While both teams have been competitive in most every game this season -- Middle's 55-0 loss to Kansas the lone exception -- FIU's defense is considered the best unit either team has, and they will present a stiff challenge to the Blue Raiders' offense. A win for either team keeps them alive in the conference title game race at 2-1 and would set the tone for a positive second half of the season.
Liberty vs. Kennesaw State
Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 7 p.m.
Location: Fifth Third Stadium -- Kennesaw, Georgia
TV: CBS Sports Network [Channel finder]
Live stream: CBSSports.com | Mobile: CBS Sports App
Spread: Liberty -10.5

After a slow start to the year with a loss to James Madison and a near disaster against Gardner-Webb, Liberty has hit its stride and has started to look like the Liberty of old the past four weeks. Jamey Chadwell's group has been terrific on defense all season, and the offense has started to hit its stride thanks to a dynamic rushing attack headlined by Kam Davis. Kennesaw State, meanwhile, has struggled this season after making the conference title game in 2025. The Owls have fallen off tremendously as an offense, ranking outside the top 100 in the nation in scoring, and they'll need to produce their best to challenge this Flames defense.
UMass vs. UConn
Date: Friday, Oct. 23 | Time: 7 p.m.
Location: Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field -- East Hartford, Connecticut
TV: CBS Sports Network [Channel finder]
Live stream: CBSSports.com | Mobile: CBS Sports App
Spread: UConn -14.5

UMass started the season with its biggest win ever over Rutgers and got to 4-0, but the Minutemen have dropped three straight in MAC play as the offense has struggled since losing quarterback Pop Watson to injury. The positive for UMass is that, even on their losing streak, they've been competitive in the last two games and continue to look like a vastly improved program. Still, they're a healthy two-touchdown underdog on the road to a UConn team that's fresh off a bye week and is probably better than their 3-3 record would indicate. The Huskies have lost two heartbreakers to Miami (OH) and Syracuse in recent weeks before a get-right win at Temple, and will have their sights set on getting back above .500 in a game that has far more intrigue than expected.
Western Michigan vs. Toledo
Date: Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time: 12 p.m.
Location: Glass Bowl -- Toledo, Ohio
TV: CBS Sports Network [Channel finder]
Live stream: CBSSports.com | Mobile: CBS Sports App
Spread: Toledo -3

This could end up as the game of the year in the MAC. Toledo bounced back from a dismal loss to Buffalo to wreck Eastern Michigan on the road to reassert themselves as a favorite in the conference. John Alan Richter has been incredible taking over as the starter for the Rockets, and Mike Jacobs has quickly proven himself as a coach jumping from the FCS level. Western Michigan remained undefeated in MAC play with a win over rivals Central Michigan last week, and while the Broncos aren't quite as dangerous as they seemed after nearly beating Michigan in Week 1, they are firmly among the best in the MAC. These two, plus Ohio, seem like the class of the MAC and the winner in the Glass Bowl will have a leg up in the conference title game race.
North Texas vs. Navy
Date: Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time: 3:30 p.m.
Location: Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium -- Annapolis, Maryland
TV: CBS Sports Network [Channel finder]
Live stream: CBSSports.com | Mobile: CBS Sports App
Spread: North Texas -2

After coming up just short in a shootout at UTSA last week, Navy heads home desperate for a win but having to deal with one of the American's best teams in North Texas. Despite losing so much this offseason with Eric Morris leaving for Oklahoma State and bringing a lot of players with him in the portal, the Mean Green have reloaded and are right back in the mix for the American conference title game. Given the way both of these teams can score (and the struggles they've had defensively), this game has all the makings of a back-and-forth shootout.
Utah State vs. Texas State
Date: Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time: 7:30 p.m.
Location: UFCU Stadium -- San Marcos, Texas
TV: CBS Sports Network [Channel finder]
Live stream: CBSSports.com | Mobile: CBS Sports App
Spread: Texas State -12.5

The Bobcats enjoyed their evening on CBS Sports Network so much last week that they're back again, this time hosting Utah State. Texas State rolled up 66 on Colorado State last week to improve to 3-3 and are now nearly two-touchdown favorites over the Aggies. Utah State got a needed win over Washington State two weeks ago and has had a bye to try and prepare for the high-octane Bobcats in what figures to be a clash of styles. Texas State wants to turn this into a track meet, while Utah State hopes to drag the Bobcats into the mud. Whichever team can dictate the tempo on Saturday night will have the advantage in what could be a fun one in San Marcos.

articles.headline: Vanderbilt is back in the AP Top 25. Tyler Tanner has a new cast to bring along
keyFacts: Vanderbilt is ranked No. 24 in the preseason AP Top 25, marking the team's first preseason ranking since 2015.
Star guard Tyler Tanner returns to lead a roster that has been almost entirely rebuilt with new transfers and a freshman.
The team must now prove it can integrate the new players around Tanner to justify its preseason ranking during the upcoming season.
body: Vanderbilt is No. 24 in the preseason AP Top 25, its first preseason ranking since 2015. The Commodores finished last season ranked No. 19, so the poll is not a sudden arrival from nowhere. The more interesting story is what comes next: Vanderbilt returns star guard Tyler Tanner, but the roster around him has been almost entirely rebuilt.

Tanner averaged 19.5 points, 5.1 assists and 2.4 steals per game last season. He also set Vanderbilt single-season records with 184 assists and 86 steals. Those numbers explain why he was named preseason first-team All-SEC and why the Commodores have a credible star to build around.
A ranking that depends on the pieces around Tanner

The returning group includes Tanner, Chandler Bing and Jayden Leverett. New additions include transfers Sebastian Williams-Adams, Bangot Dak and Ace Glass, along with freshman Gabe Nesmith. That is a lot of fresh chemistry to establish around a guard who spent last season making the offense run.

Tyler Tanner | Vanderbilt PG, 20 y/o -5'11" barefoot, 167, 6-4 wingspan -Advantage-creator with quickness, handle, open-floor speed. 200 rim attempts. -Good finisher, creates easier angles -Improving shotmaker, production from 3 levels -Outlier #s for small PG: 18 dunks, 12 blocks -29% PU3s, 26% floaters—needs to be better shotmaker off dribble -Short list of NBA players 170lbs or less
— Jonathan Wasserman (@NBADraftWass) October 15, 2026

Tanner’s playmaking could make the transition smoother. His 5.1 assists per game show that he can create chances for teammates, not just pile up points. But even an elite point guard needs reliable targets, screen setters and defenders around him. The first weeks will show whether Vanderbilt’s new additions can make his job easier.
No. 24 is an invitation, not a prediction

The AP ranking gives Vanderbilt early national attention, while the SEC media poll picked the Commodores sixth in the league. The difference is a reminder that a top-25 vote does not settle where a team belongs. Vanderbilt still has to prove it can turn individual talent into a dependable rotation.

That makes Tanner one of the season’s more compelling players to watch. If he can keep creating at last year’s level while the supporting cast finds its rhythm, Vanderbilt could make No. 24 look conservative. If the roster takes time to click, the preseason ranking will feel like a challenge the Commodores have to grow into.

articles.headline: Samson studio shuts down as console success ‘wasn’t enough to get the company across the finish line’
keyFacts: Liquid Swords founder Christofer Sundberg announced the studio is closing following the release of their action game Samson.
Sundberg stated that poor market conditions and business decisions prevented the studio from remaining viable despite recent console success.
The studio is currently in discussions regarding how to continue supporting the Samson game following the closure.
body: Liquid Swords, the studio behind action/adventure game Samson , will be shutting down, its founder and CEO announced today.

Christofer Sundberg revealed the news just over six months after the game launched to a 51 average score on Metacritic (I gave it a 6/10 here for Destructoid ), blaming “market conditions and some bad business decisions” for the circumstances.

Image via Liquid Swords “Liquid Swords is closing its doors,” Sundberg said in a LinkedIn post today. “I’ve done everything I can to make this succeed, and I’m very proud of what we achieved together. It’s been a hell of a ride and a lot of fun, even when the circumstances gave us very little to laugh about. Building a studio, creating Samson and releasing it on PC and consoles took an enormous amount of work from people who cared deeply about what we were making.”

In my time with Samson, the open world crime action title showed glimpses of the game it was trying to be, but was held back by mundane and repetitive gameplay, and a whole lot of bugs. The title reached a max of 2,722 players on Steam in April. In the end, it couldn’t sell what was necessary to keep the studio in business, despite a better-received console version that launched a month ago.

“The console versions met with much greater success than the PC release,” Sundberg said. “We got them out, but that success wasn’t enough to get the company across the finish line. I can look honestly at what went wrong and still be proud of what we built.”

Sundberg, known previously for his work at Avalanche Studios on games like Just Cause , says he is “in discussions with all parties involved in Liquid Swords about how we can continue to support Samson the way the game deserves,” but it appears those who worked at the studio are now out of a job.

“To everyone who worked at Liquid Swords, our partners and everyone who supported us and played Samson : thank you,” Sundberg said. “You gave us plenty of reasons to keep fighting, and the work we did together deserves to be remembered for more than how the company ended. We make mistakes, we learn, we fall, we rise up, we move on. That’s sometimes a painful process, especially when it affects people you care about, but I refuse to give up. I never give up.”

articles.headline: Tottenham v Coventry: Premier League – live
keyFacts: Tottenham Hotspur secured their first league win of the season by defeating Coventry City 3-1.
James Maddison scored in his return from a long-term injury, with Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies also contributing goals for Tottenham.
Tottenham faces a series of upcoming matches against Chelsea, Crystal Palace, Leeds, Ipswich, Sunderland, and Fulham.
body: James Maddison scored a beauty on his return from long-term injury, with Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies also on target as Spurs won in the league for the first time this season
“How many teams manage to double both their points and goals scored in a single day in mid-October?” wonders Phil Moseley.

Yup, and Spurs have some winnable games coming up too. Chelsea away this weekend will be tricky but then comes Palace home, Leeds away, Ipswich home, Sunderland away, Fulham home. We’ll have a decent idea of the kind of season they’ll have at the end of that run.

A terrific night for Spurs, Maddison making a scoring return, Kulusevski also coming back, and a first league win of the season. They didn’t play especially well but they’ll be better for this, while Coventry again showed enough to suggest they’ve a chance of staying up.
90+7 min The third goal is, in a way, just reward for trying to score it – last week, Spurs benefited from a side too scared to pursue a clincher, a mistake they’ve not made themselves.
GOAL! Tottenham Hotspur 3-1 Coventry City (Davies 90+6)

After 148 days, Tottenham are going to win a league game! Tel does well to take time out of the game and, when his cross is cleared to the edge, an important touch from Solanke allows Davis to swipe a low trivela that arcs just inside the near post. Relief inside the ground!
90+3 min Coventry opt not to launch a long throw, instead putting a pass into the box and keeping the attack alive well before Mason-Clark wins a corner.
90+1 min From a seemingly impossible position close to the by-line and Van Hecke in front of him, Mason-Clark drives over a cross that Awoniyi attacks … but can’t quite reach.
89 min Davies leaves one on Kesler-Hatden and Hamer sends the free-kick into the box, Thomas up, but Spurs clear and Kulusevski leads the counter alone, crossing way beyond the far post to no one.

86 min After Maddison’s goal another affirming moment for Spurs, Marmoush going down with what might be cramp, Kulusevski replacing him. He gets the big welcome he deserves; let’s hope he can stay fit now, because if he can, he’s a proper player. Oh and Tel also comes on, with Kudus going off.

84 min Caoventry are now building the play with four men on the last line and Mason-Clark lays back for Dasilva whose cross isn’t bad, but Rudoni can’t quite crane his neck-muscles enough to head at goal.
83 min Spurs keep it well, burning time, but I bet there are some fans who half want them to concede now, so they’ve time to seek a winner. Such is the torment of a low-scoring sport.

81 min Davies nashes down the left and Spurs again move the ball right to Kudus. Again, he comes infield but this time he crosses and, when the clearance reaches Fernandes, he curls a sidefooter into Rushworth’s arms.

80 min Good work from Tonali, who weaves by a couple of challenges in midfield before the ball makes its way out to Kudus, who dips infield to open the angle for a curler, before sending his effort over the bar.

79 min Tonali humps out of play, yet more evidence Spurs are feeling this, and if they can’t rely on him to keep the head, who can they rely on? But they do get the long throw away and set off on the attack.

77 min Thomas-Asante intercepts a poor pass from Gallagher and seeks Rudoni, who can’t quite take the ball away from Van Hecke. Still, though, Spurs look nervous already, a feeling that’ll only intensify as we get nearer full time.
74 min I guess whatever colour Coventry’s kit is, it looks like what it’s meant to be. The first time I saw Sunderland’s pink Elvis top, not one part of me believed it not to be leisurewear.
73 min Van Ewijk robs Kudus deep inside the Spurs half and flights a cross to the back post … just over Rudoni. Coventry are playing with the belief that they can equalise.
70 min Changes for Spurs, Davies for Robertson, Gallagher for Maddison – who enjoys the acclaim of the crowd as he departs – and Fernandes for the cramping Tosin. I guess they’ll go to 4-2-3-1.

68 min Coventry are building a bit of pressure, a cross-kick into the box allowing Thomas to leap all over Gray, heading back across and forcing Van de Ven to diving head away. Already, it’s a bit panicked and, with so long left, that is not the way spurs want to be defending.

67 min “Completely agree about how horrible Parma Violets taset,” says David Wall. “However they’re very useful when ground up if you want to colour the purple layer of a rainbow cake and haven’t got the right food dye. Fortunately the violet flavour is subtle enough that you can’t actually taste it in the cake.”
That is good information, thanks – though would one not use Fizzers to get the same effect and a bit more action?

65 min Coventry are indeed getting Rudoni into the game, as we said they’d have to; he’s drifting about unchecked and lasers a pass into the box that Awoniyi can’t quite get on the end of. As long as it stays 2-1, Coventry have a decent chance of sneaking a point.
64 min A fine long pass from Van Hecke sets Solanke at Thomas, right side of the box, and he chops inside well only to see the shooting lanes closed down, thwacking an effort that’s blocked.

62 min Credit to Spurs, by the way, who didn’t feel sorry for themselves after conceding but went after a second goal – which they ought really to have done straight after their first. They’ve not made that mistake this time, though, pushing hard for a clinching third.

60 min There was proper contact but VAR deems it accidental, which I think is a bit of a touch for Spurs. I guess it’s one of those you’re vexed if you score it and it’s chalked off, but you’re also vexed if it’s scored against you and it isn’t, so it makes some sort of sense to go with the original call.
ANOTHER LOVELY GOAL! Tottenham Hotspur 2-1 Coventry City (Marmoush 59)

Marmoush spins Van Ewijk, introducing elbow to nose in the process, feints the shot then, stepping inside, punches a curler from 20 yards that Rushworth gets hands to but can’t keep out. That’s his first goal for Spurs, but will VAR disallow it?

52 min We said Spurs would need a second goal and they’re seeking one, Kudus hitting the line and cutting back a decent cross, half-cleared to Tonali, charging in … and he hammers an effort that flies over the top.

articles.headline: So What Are We Supposed To Take Away From You Can See Everything?
keyFacts: Nathan Fielder’s documentary You Can See Everything examines the life of Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes before she surrendered to federal custody.
The film explores Holmes's relationship with her partner, Billy Evans, and questions whether she is a victim of trauma or a calculated deceiver.
The documentary does not provide definitive answers, leaving viewers to navigate uncertainty regarding Holmes's true personality and motivations.
body: So, You Can See Everything, huh? A few of us here at Kotaku saw Nathan Fielder’s documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, the founder of Theranos, a health tech company that was shut down after Holmes was convicted of defrauding investors in 2018. The basis of the accusations was that the company’s signature device, which Theranos claimed could accurately conduct a vast assortment of blood tests on a single drop of blood, didn’t work as investors were led to believe. The film documents her final weeks with her partner and children before having to surrender herself into federal custody in Bryan, Texas.

Kenneth Shepard: And that’s only half of the Everything we See in this movie. So Ash, before we get into all there is to unpack, tell me, what was your knowledge of both Holmes and of Fielder’s work leading up to seeing this movie?

Ash Parrish: So most of my initial exposure to Nathan Fielder had been against my will. My first run-in with his work was the first season of his HBO show The Rehearsal where I felt for him both kinship and revulsion. I was fascinated and amused by the Inception-like depth to which he would pursue a subject and the results that would produce in his human guinea pigs. I’ve been hooked ever since. Less so, though, with Nathan for You which I have only seen bits and pieces of because my husband thinks itâs fucking hilarious. That show makes me want to crawl out of my flesh. Far less endearing than The Rehearsal.

As for Elizabeth Holmes, I think I saw some of the initial documentaries that had come out about her after her legal convictions but that was it. I didn’t see and didn’t care about The Dropout. But I knew her in broad strokes.

I think what lit my brain on fire with You Can See Everything is I know Fielder can get weird, and that the weirder he gets, the more human a story emerges, either from his subjects or himself (I’m thinking of the time he got a pilot’s license in the purest distillation of commitment to the bit). I wanted to see him work his eldritch neurodivergent truth powers on her to see what shakes out and HO BOY.

KS: I have avoided a lot of Fielder’s work because secondhand embarrassment makes me viscerally uncomfortable in a way that my therapist and I have had many conversations about. I watched the first episode of The Rehearsal and was like, “Oh, if it’s only going to get worse from here I have to tap out.”

For Holmes, I had only vague recollections of what happened with her and Theranos when the trailers came out because that was absolutely something outside of my orbit. I think I saw those stories coming out and kind of thought, “Ah, an American medical company being deceitful. For me, it was Tuesday.” Never watched The Dropout or really thought much about her again, to the point where when I first saw the You Can See Everything trailer I didn’t immediately recognize her. However, that trailer with Nathan and Elizabeth being inches away from each other’s face and heâs straight up asking her if she’s being deceitful sent chills down my spine.

I think anyone who has ever dealt with a narcissist or pathological liar has had a conversation like that, where they’re looking someone in the eye who, whether they truly internally believe it or not, is so committed to the âtruthâ they’re trying to put out that it’s almost unnerving. I was immediately brought back to a conversation I had in a coffee shop with an ex of mine in college who was very obviously lying to me, and he had to have known that I knew he was lying because I had literally laid out the facts of a situation in a way he could not feasibly debunk, and yet he dug his heels in, and I had that same expression Fielder has in the trailer of just pure annoyed disbelief, and I straight up just said “Why are you doing this?” Like, why are you committing so hard to this when the facts of the matter are laid out here. And so from this scene alone of two people where the dynamic seemed to be one person caught in dishonesty and another person just looking at them and trying to read why they’re acting like this, I felt like I had to see this movie almost as a form of catharsis for a nearly decade-old event. I don’t think I necessarily got that, and obviously after seeing it in the context of the movie, that initial scene is a bit more layered than it originally seemed. But it got me to watch something I would have probably skipped otherwise.

AP: How do you feel about Holmes now after seeing the full film? I’m honestly less concerned about her flavor of narcissistic pathology because she, for better or worse, is serving her court-mandated restitution for that. Meanwhile Billy Fucking Evans is a free man breathing free air.

KS: That is kinda the big question of the movie, right? Like, ultimately, yeah, Holmes is doing her time, I don’t frankly feel any sympathy for the people she may or may not have ripped off (motherfucking Assassin’s Creed villain Henry Kissinger was on the Theranos board?), so the fraud of it all doesn’t get me. I do think, and obviously all of this is couched as “the movie presents this in a particular way, and that is what we have to cast judgments about,” You Can See Everything does make her a sympathetic figure, and simultaneously makes a whole show of acknowledging the folly of doing so. Because I did genuinely feel for Elizabeth Holmes âthe characterâ as she is portrayed on film. Fielder goes out of his way to show how the slightest gap in what someone says and how it is perceived can lead to a communication shit storm, and whether or not I believe that Holmes actually doesn’t understand those nuances is immaterial to how much I have seen that bullshit manifest every day as a person who works with words on the internet. A headline that people react to because of what they think it means rather than what it actually means is something we see every day in this line of work. So I think the movie showing things like the famous “Who’s on First?” comedy routine is effective in communicating this hypothetical disconnect. But then yeah, is it all an act? Is the way she and Evans basically say the exact same things to him when he’s interviewing them independently a sign that these two are ironclad con artists and Fielder maybe got too close to see it all objectively? Again, those are questions the movie asks and is at least upfront about.

I think if Holmes was being honest with Fielder during his prison visit about her knowledge of all the various insane things Evans has been doing both before and during her sentence, then who am I to tell her not to date and have children with a red-pilled Silicon Valley fuckboy when she seems happy doing so? If she didn’t know about all those things, she most certainly will now, and if she chooses to raise a family and a business with him and is truly not in any distress about it, then is this just a rich person’s version of “girl who stays with her shitty boyfriend and makes excuses for himâ?

And even that kneejerk reaction feels dismissive because anyone who’s been in an abusive relationship will tell you that you will romanticize it until you can’t anymore. A man putting an AI mock-up of his partner on the internet and just shrugging at the idea of it being used for nefarious reasons? Immediate breakup. That man has no respect for you. The movie outright asks the Stockholm Syndrome question and just kinda feels like it’s hit a wall. Which, you know, ending a movie on “We don’t have a satisfactory answer to all these questions” is as valid a conclusion as any. You can see everything, but you’ll never truly know everything.

AP: Yeah I was going to ask: Do you think she’s aware enough to know she should be in distress? My alarm bells as a person with experience with narcissistic / abusive people were ringing off the whole scene with the eggs. But even then I question it because that’s a weird way for someone to whisk eggs. Does Elizabeth know that? Was that scene constructed to reinforce the narrative that she’s just too naive, too neurodivergent, and needs someone like Evans to steer her directly?

And her poor children, she had them just before she was sent away. In an interview with Fielder in WIRED, he shared that she patently did not think she was going to jail. And I can’t help but wonder if the sympathy having two little kids running around encouraged was part of a grander scheme. “You can’t send me to jail, look I have babies. Think of them.”

KS: Same. I was at the Alamo Drafthouse watching it so I wasn’t about to so much as whisper to my friends sitting next to me during the eggs scene lest their snipers take me out, but I immediately sat straight up in my chair and looked at them like “what the fuck?” And that wasn’t even remotely close to the most fucked-up thing Evans would do during the whole movie. The more charitable read that this is just their dynamic and they’re both content with it is a valid one, but from a filmmaking perspective You Can See Everything does seem to lean into the narrative that something is amiss here from the outset. They both were supposedly okay with this entire documentary project, but she is remarkably open about it, whereas he’s the one who gets cagey about answering questions or Fielder talking to her family for too long.

There’s also the added layer of, which I didn’t know going in, her father bringing up that she was raped at Stanford, which is the kind of world-shattering thing that can completely skew your relationships with other people. So again, I feel like the movie wants me to at least consider the charitable and sympathetic angle that maybe she wasn’t deceitful, but instead was someone who has been traumatized by her lived experience and now sees the world through a more neurodivergent lens. The human part of me wants to see it that way, but everything else that’s happening around it makes me hesitant to do so. Like even shit where she’s like “I never let people see me cry” and then seems to just start crying on command. Could Elizabeth Holmes be a neurodivergent woman who has dealt with a lot of trauma, is naive, got in over her head, and is also possibly a pathological liar? Does the founder of Theranos contain multitudes like Walt Whitman once said?

AP: I don’t think those two things are at odds with each other. And this is a way to help one reinforce the other. I believe, like any ND person, myself included, that effective communication is fraught. I don’t, can’t, believe that it could be SO impenetrable to her that she doesnât grasp why people interpreted the âcanâ in “This machine can run all kinds of tests” as meaning what Fielder said it meant.Â
If that kind of miscommunication gaffe is the hill you’re choosing to die onâ¦
And it’s made more sinister by Evans in that moment being like “See the kind of whimsical spirit she is!” in this gross paternalistic kind of way.

KS: It is the weird game Fielder has to play here that he does, to some extent, have to at the very least interrogate those claims and ideas in good faith, no matter how absurd they might sound. Yet even when the movie is connecting these dots of how language can be interpreted in various ways and that she simply sees the world differently and your facts and logic are just trying to diminish her shine, the shadow of a New York Times article that claims Holmes called her public-facing persona a “character” she created looms over everything, and the quoteâs validity never debunked in this movie despite Holmes disputing that she said it. So regardless of whatever earnest beliefs she claims to hold, the entire thing is suspect and everyone, Fielder and the viewers, has to live with the constant uncertainty.

Then yeah, you have Evans propping all this up while also being more forthright in being a fucking con artist so when any of those aspects of her alleged personality show up I’m like, “how deep does this charade go?”
AP: Fielder himself has some suspicion hanging over him too. There was more than one moment in the film where I’m clawing at my husband like “HE BETTER NOT KISS HER.”
Then there’s the whole moment about “breaking his rule” to never go in the cold water. And that winds up being the final shot of the film.

KS: That thread is interesting because it’s one of the points in the movie where it kind of moves away from typical documentary-style storytelling and into a more traditional, non-documentary narrative. Because the first time we see that is when he goes back to the beach house years later and is looking out to the beach almost wistfully, like he’s distracted. This is when Dropout actor Amanda Seyfried has shown up after being roped into all this, and the movie starts to become more like an overtly authored thing, and Fielder comes into this place with the intention of illustrating his own thought process. Which, you know, Seyfried even asks him at the end if he might have hidden something, kept something out of the movie that would have made Holmes look bad, if he’d grown to care for her, which yeah, the shot of them swimming together seems to communicate that yes, he did grow to care for her and could have obscured something about her, whether intentionally or subconsciously. Whether that means he omitted something groundbreaking or not, he may have, at some point in the project, grown to sympathize with her, which is, in my interpretation, why we get the cut of the film that we do.

Which I can imagine is going to get on some people’s nerves because I do think if youâre coming into this movie in the hopes of finding out what “really” happened with Theranos and who Elizabeth Holmes really is, you’re probably not going to get that. To me, a lot of the movie’s underlying thesis is that the pursuit of trying to truly know someone, even someone who claims to be an open book, is a losing game. Everything we know about a person is experienced through a distorted lens, whether that be a projection of how they want to be perceived, our own lived experience informing how we interpret something (like someone’s romantic relationship), or, in this case, a documentary by someone who seems to worry he has become compromised from the objective truth of a person. Even if someone is completely honest with you on just like, a factual level, experiences with people who are less forthright mean we will likely always view them with some level of suspicion. And in some cases that’s healthy, I suppose. It keeps us vigilant and protects us from being overly trusting.

AP: I don’t think people are approaching You Can See Everything with the intent to have answered for good and all the question of whether Elizabeth Holmes is lying. I really do think the appeal is to watch two master manipulators have a manipulate-off and to see the depths to which Fielder goes trying to untangle his own feelings about that. In which case, mission pretty well accomplished.

KS: I think thereâs going to be at least some fraction of the audience who might be unaware of Fielder’s work but remember Holmes’ case and are hoping to get some sort of real insight into it all that will not be found here. Because yes, even though the first half is largely presented as a documentary, it’s not until the second half, the half that they deliberately obfuscated from promotional materials, that the Fielder of it all really comes out. Which, we have actually somehow gotten this deep into this conversation and not really touched on. While the first half of the movie documents Holmes’ final days before turning herself in, the second half, which picks up years after the fact, is where Fielder miraculously works through limitations that would have been documentary-ending roadblocks by bringing in Amanda Seyfried, who portrayed Holmes in The Dropout, to perform reenactments of some segments Fielder wasn’t able to film, while also becoming very invested in figuring out the truth herself in a way that was also really fascinating to watch unfold.

Now, I was kind of bracing myself for something like this, as she had been a bit cagey about whether she was in the documentary when asked in interviews, and I’d seen theories long before the movie was out that Seyfried would be involved in some way, though they were a little off-base in some ways. How did you react when Seyfried showed up in the flesh?
AP: I had no idea she was involved in the movie, but I knew the moment she popped up he’d have her engage in some kind of recreation. “This is The Rehearsal season three.”

And it honestly felt good to watch her watch what weâd seen and see her fall into the same trap I did. At the beginning you feel for that woman, you see her, Seyfried, recognize in real time the kind of bastard Evans looks like. Then we all get to go on the same emotional trip together when Fielder reveals the money aspect to her and subsequently us, that Evans had approached A24 executives about getting paid for their participation and convinced them to agree to it!! and how Holmes may not have known about that.

The back half of the movie unteasing that aspect was a wild ride. I’m grasping and clawing at my partner, desperate for Fielder’s phone to ring because I wanted him to have a conversation without Evans present to direct (or pretending to direct).

And I think that’s when, through Seyfriedâs parroting of Holmesâ words in elaborate pantomime, the phrase “building monuments to love” comes up and that’s where it all falls apart for me. That’s such an odd, specific thing to say. And the fact that both Holmes and Evans said it in such different situations, tells me they really did have a fucking script.

KS: In some ways Seyfried felt like the audience stand-in because Fielder’s not gonna be like “fuck this man, actually,” so thanks to her for her service. And to have someone on camera for Fielder to talk to more candidly was nice because the first half of the movie does have to exist in this specific setup where he can say or do whatever he wants but he’s trying not to interfere too much with the day to day. So Seyfriedâs segment of just talking about what he’s seen and what he suspects could be happening feels like the first time the movie really breaks out of that reality. It felt like that was where the movie was pivoting into a sort of “oh, so here’s the actual story here” phase, and that story is that Evans is a bastard who is controlling this woman, owning and manipulating her image while sheâs in prison, and Fielder may have stumbled into something that he needs Seyfriedâs help to communicate on film.

It was cathartic to see her just kind of lay Evans out for the kind of person he was by, I guess, being a woman with opinions he didn’t like in the room, and kudos to her for not jumping across that kitchen table and beating his ass. But also, as much as she was ready to fight on behalf of another woman, she also kind of has to deal with the fallout of her own part in all of this in that her show, even if she believed herself to have some safe distance by not having interacted with Holmes directly, had some impact on how Holmes was perceived. She gets defensive and says “we were making TV,” but the average person doesn’t grasp that biopics and the like are “based on” reality. Again, sort of another example of what is said and what is perceived having consequences, even if whatâs being communicated is misunderstood or interpreted in ways the ones doing the communicating didn’t intend. Is Holmes actually experiencing the harassment she mentions? Nobody knows, because everything she says feels suspect, especially as, like you said, it really feels like she and Evans have some kind script memorized about how they will talk about and present their lives to anyone outside of them.

One last thing I do want to bring up, because I’m sure we could go on forever extrapolating everything in this movie, but to kinda wrap up things, something I did want to talk about was the title: You Can See Everything. On its face, that’s almost like a quote from Holmes, inviting everyone into her home to see who she actually is, but I do think the movie itself completely recontextualizes the title when Holmes and Fielder have a whole conversation about the meaning of the word “can.” You hypothetically can do anything, but that doesn’t mean you actually will. Then, I saw someone point out that in a lot of the movie’s promotional material like trailers and posters, the world Everything is positioned to the left of the You Can See, so it could be read as “Everything You Can See” instead. And I just want to point out that if either of those things were intended that way, that’s some damn fine wordplay and the kind of shit that makes someone whisper “fuck” to themself when they think of it. Because it sums up the whole movie. It presents itself pretty straightforwardly but there’s all this other context that means you can’t quite trust it.

Ultimately, I’m glad I saw it, and maybe it is my lack of Fielder experience that made me read it as something other than a sort of manipulation-off. I left feeling less like I understood either Fielder or Holmes, and more like Iâd just been made to think a lot about the futility of trying to actually know who anyone truly is, and the degrees of discomfort inherent in living with that. And, ultimately, I think I did see enough to know that I don’t need to know any more about Elizabeth Holmes and her shitty-ass red-pilled boyfriend.

AP: Oh I definitely don’t need to see anymore of her or her baby daddy. And that’s a great point with the “can” that I didn’t put that together, considering a big moment in the film hinges on that flimsy little word. Good catch.
You, too, can see everything by seeing You Can See Everything in theaters now.

articles.headline: There's a new free hi-res music streaming app on iPhone and Android with no ads and no subscription
keyFacts: Audiophile.fm launched a free mobile app for Android and iOS that streams CD-quality and hi-res internet radio without requiring a subscription or account.
Creator Bojan Vidanovic stated the app offers handpicked lossless stations spanning genres like jazz, classical, rock, and electronic.
Future plans include adding features like equalization, Google Cast, and AirPlay, while keeping the core app free.
body: - Audiophile.fm now has an app for Android and iOS 26 or later, in addition to its web version
- It's a free streaming radio service, and all music is CD quality or hi-res
- No subscription needed, no account, and no in-app ads

If you're looking for an audio alternative to ad-stuffed and/or expensive subscription music services, Audiophile.fm could be just what you're looking for. It's a free and ad-free player for internet radio stations that stream in CD quality or higher, and it just launched an app for iOS and Android, having already been available in your web browser.
While Macs aren't officially supported, you can grab the iPhone version from the Mac App Store. I've done that on my Mac, and can confirm it runs perfectly on macOS 27.

The app was created by Bojan Vidanovic, who explained on r/BudgetAudiophile that "I wanted an easier way to find and listen to lossless radio stations. It brings together handpicked stations streaming in FLAC, from CD-quality to Hi-Res options across jazz, classical, rock, electronic, and more."
The response has been really positive, and having tried it, I'd say that's because it's a really nice app.
Free hi-res audio streaming. What's the catch?

The catch is: there is no catch, as far as I can see. The app and website connects you to internet radio stations, who presumably have all the necessary permissions and licenses in place to ensure the artists they play get paid. The app itself is ad-free, but some of the stations play ads to pay the bills, naturally.

The joy here is serendipity: there's no algorithm serving you up endless variations of the songs you already like, so you can end up with truly random listening: for example I've just gone from Daft Punk to French jazz to Underworld deep cuts to the new Beck album to Culture Club to, er, Alien Ant Farm.

And the sound quality is consistently excellent because all of the stations are broadcasting in FLAC at CD quality or better. I've listened to a whole bunch on my favorite headphones and the only one that sounded horrible was playing Alien Ant Farm.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.

This is very much a work in progress — things like equalization, Google Cast and AirPlay are on the to-do list — but it's a very impressive starting point and Bojan is actively seeking feedback on Reddit. The plan is apparently to keep the core app free and monetize it with additional paid features at some point in the future.

Obviously, this is no replacement for the likes of Spotify, if you're an audiophile who gets frustrated with the discovery options of the big music services, this could give you a great alternative: a wide mix of music, all in quality to show off what the best wired headphones combined with a nice headphone DAC can do.

body: Trump slams Zelenskyy amid Russia sanctions rift and says ‘somebody else’ should negotiate for Ukraine - live
President facing criticism for his move to waive sanctions for Russia as a new poll by Reuters shows only 31% of Americans approve of his performance in office
'It's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine': Trump slams Zelenskyy and defends lifting Russian sanctions
Trump again rebuked the idea that his move to waive sanctions for Russia last week was ultimately to hand Moscow a win.

“I’m supporting stopping the war between Russia and Ukraine,” Trump told reporters. “Frankly, Zelenskyy is not helping matters much. I think he doesn’t want to stop it, but I want to see people not die.”
In response to Zelenskyy saying that the US president is on the “wrong side of history”, Trump snapped back.

“If he would have listened to me, he would have made a much better deal a long time ago, and he’d have a million people living from his side,” Trump said. “I think it’s time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine …. Very little land has moved, but a million people, a tremendous number of people, are dead.”
Vance speech disrupted by protester shouting 'release the Epstein files'
A protester in North Carolina disrupted a speech by JD Vance, the US vice-president, in North Caroline on Monday, shouting “Release the Epstein files! God bless our children!” before being led away.

The protester, who was positioned directly behind Vance during a midterm campaign rally in support of Republican candidates, was seen on a live video stream standing up and shouting about 10 minutes into the vice-president’s speech.
As the man was led away the crowd booed the interruption, and chanted “U!S!A!”
Vance then attempted to joke that the man, a person of color who spoke with an American accent, must be an undocumented immigrant.

“Ladies and gentlemen, I’m going to have to amend something I said earlier. I said that we have had zero illegal border crossings in the United States of America,” Vance said to laughter from the crowd. “But one isn’t bad, right?”
New Reuters poll shows Trump's approval rating dropping to a record low
A new poll by Reuters shows that only 31% of Americans approve of Donald Trump’s performance in office, a percentage point lower than the survey from two weeks ago and a record low for the president.
It comes as Trump embarks on another campaign sprint to help beleaguered Republicans in competitive midterm races.
When asked which party they would vote for if the elections were held today, 47% of registered voters in the nationwide poll picked Democrats, while 35% chose Republicans.

Ahead of leaving for a campaign rally in Wichita, Kansas, Donald Trump again claimed – without evidence – that the riots throughout France were due to mass migration.

“I told Emmanuel [Macron], you should close up your borders,” the US president said. “I’ve known him for probably eight or nine years. I told him as soon as I met him, I said, ‘you’re making a big mistake’. We closed our borders. He didn’t.”

Attorneys for Mahmoud Khalil, the former Columbia University student who has become the symbol of the Trump administration’s crusade against pro-Palestinian speech, have petitioned the US supreme court to review his case – the final chapter in a months-long legal saga that could determine countless foreign citizens’ ability to challenge their detention by US immigration authorities in federal court.

Khalil, a US permanent resident who was born in a Palestinian refugee camp in Syria, was arrested in his Columbia housing in March 2025, the first of several foreign students and scholars the Trump administration targeted over their advocacy for Palestinian rights. He was detained for more than three months in an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility in Louisiana before a federal judge in New Jersey, where he had been briefly held before ICE moved him, ordered him released while his immigration process proceeds.

“This fight is not only about whether I get to stay in this country, it’s really about whether anyone in this country can speak out for Palestinians without being punished for it,” Khalil said during a press conference on Monday.
The US departments of state, justice and homeland security did not respond to requests for comment.
The government has cited an obscure McCarthy-era law to argue that Khalil and the other scholars’ pro-Palestinian expression posed a threat to US foreign policy objectives.

So far, no court has fully weighed in on the constitutionality of the law, with legal arguments instead focused on whether district courts have the authority to order people released from immigration detention while their immigration cases are under way. Khalil’s attorneys and immigrants rights advocates warn that if the supreme court rules the district courts lack such authority, that would effectively result in people the government has detained unconstitutionally to languish in immigration detention with no recourse, potentially for months or years.

The justice department announced the arrest of 28 legal permanent residents in California “who are charged in criminal complaints with federal crimes, including that they fraudulently registered to vote in US elections, electoral contests in which most of them cast illegal and fraudulently obtained ballots”. Non-citizen voting is extremely rare, andthe 28 who have allegedly committed crimes, would be an exceptionally small fraction of the 174 million people who were registered to vote in the 2024 presidential election.The arrests come just days after the administration sued the Golden state, to prevent it from counting mail-in ballots from people the federal government has allegedly identified as “likely” noncitizens.

New polling also shows that a majority (66%) of Americans believe Trump is using the presidency to enrich himself. Looking at that data from the Washington Post and ABC even further, 34% of Republicans believe Trump is enriching himself – a 12-point jump from last September. More here

Meanwhile, Trump heads to Kansas today to kick off a seven-state campaign blitz this week in parts of the country he carried in 2024, as unexpectedly tight races in GOP strongholds stoke fears of sweeping Democratic gains in next month’s midterms. With 15 days until the 3 November vote, Trump’s rally on the outskirts of Wichita aims to shore up the incumbent Republican senator Roger Marshall, who is locked in a dead heat with his Democratic opponent Adam Hamilton. He’ll follow up with rallies in the Carolinas, Iowa, Florida, Georgia and Michigan over the next six days.

On Monday, congressman Suhas Subramanyam, a Virginia Democrat, said his office in Leesburg received an envelope “containing a suspicious substance” and staff were “promptly evacuated”. Similarly, in Maine, Democratic representative Chellie Pingree said that her office also received “a suspicious letter consistent with those received by many other congressional and election offices in recent days”.

In a bipartisan call with GOP Senator Thom Tillis and Senator Richard Blumenthal, a Democrat, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine’s access to Starlink satellite services “remain degraded” and “disruptions to US intelligence sharing” persist, when it comes to the “early warning of Russian ballistic missile launches”. Last week, the two lawmakers called on the Pentagon’s inspector general to investigate Ukraine’s disruptions accessing Starshield – the military version of Starlink’s satellite network built for governments and defense agencies – and in a statement today they said that Zelenskyy reiterated his “willingness to halt strikes on Russian energy facilities as President Trump has proposed, but only if [Vladimir] Putin agrees to the same”.

A man who heckled the Democratic candidate for Senate Abdul El-Sayed and demanded he disavow the Muslim Brotherhood at a Michigan town hall is a former aide to the Republican senator Josh Hawley, according to congressional staff records.

At the event on Saturday, an attender who gave his name only as “Tommy” shouted from the crowd, asking whether El-Sayed would disavow the movement. El-Sayed answered: “Sure, yeah, absolutely,” then turned the question around, asking whether the man assumed he wouldn’t.

Tommy said he had simply not heard El-Sayed reject the Muslim Brotherhood, one of the Arab world’s oldest and most influential Islamist movements. Under Trump the US has moved to designate certain chapters of the group as foreign terrorist organizations.

Over nearly five minutes at the town hall, El-Sayed pointed to how the question shouted by Tommy carried an implication of “dual loyalty”, comparing it with the doubts once raised about John F Kennedy’s Catholicism, and told the room he was running for the Senate and “happen[s] to be Muslim”.

He then asked Tommy whether he would disavow any attempt to read religious doctrine into American law. Tommy said he would not. El-Sayed answered that it was Tommy who needed to understand the constitution, drawing cheers, and the man left the room.

The questioner has since been identified as Thomas Teepell, whose staff records show he joined Hawley’s office as an intern in 2023 and rose to operations director before leaving in February. He then became political director for Philip Sarnecki’s Kansas gubernatorial campaign. Sarnecki lost the Republican primary on 4 August.
Teepell is the son of the Republican strategist Timmy Teepell, a longtime adviser to Hawley and the former Louisiana governor Bobby Jindal. The Handbasket first reported the identification.
The question echoes a line of attack that Republicans have tried to push against El-Sayed for weeks, including when Rogers raised alleged Brotherhood ties during one of their debates.
Zelenskyy tells lawmakers that Starlink services 'remain degraded'; US intelligence sharing disruptions persist

Last week, the two lawmakers called on the Pentagon’s inspector general to investigate Ukraine’s disruptions accessing Starshield – the military version of Starlink’s satellite network built for governments and defense agencies – and in a statement today they said that Zelenskyy reiterated his “willingness to halt strikes on Russian energy facilities as President Trump has proposed, but only if [Vladimir] Putin agrees to the same”.

Zelenskyy’s call with Washington lawmakers comes after he said that Ukraine did not receive a warning from the US about an impending Russian missile attack on Sunday evening, as my colleague Andrew Roth reports from Kyiv. On Friday, Trump waived a sweeping package of sanctions on Russia – a move he claimed was to prevent driving Russia “away from the bargaining table”.

We’re getting word from more US representatives that their offices have been sent suspicious letters.

Similarly, in Maine, Democratic congresswoman Chellie Pingree said that her office alsoreceived “a suspicious letter consistent with those received by many other congressional and election offices in recent days”.

A reminder that last week the FBI and the US Postal Inspection Service were investigating letters sent to state officials and election offices across the country containing an “unknown substance”. On Thursday, the office of Arizona’s secretary of state received a similar envelope that was opened by staff, prompting a hazmat and law enforcement response as well as evacuations at the state capitol.
In Oklahoma, state troopers determined the substance mailed to the Oklahoma state capitol complex was non-hazardous.

In Cook county, Illinois, an envelope containing only white powder was sent to Maria Pappas, the treasurer, on Thursday morning, prompting a response from local emergency responders and law enforcement.
The powder turned out to be baking powder, Pappas’s office confirmed to the Guardian.
Department of Justice announces arrest of 28 legal permanent residents over alleged voter fraud

The Department of Justice has announced the arrest of 28 legal permanent residents or green card holders in California “who are charged in criminal complaints with federal crimes, including that they fraudulently registered to vote in US elections, electoral contests in which most of them cast illegal and fraudulently obtained ballots”. (A reminder that, as the DoJ press release says, these are allegations, and not yet proven.)

Ahead of next month’s midterms, the Trump administration has escalated its fight with the Golden state, warning on Friday that local officials who process and tabulate ballots submitted by suspected noncitizen voters are putting themselves at risk of criminal investigation and potential prosecution.

That threat came just a day after the administration sued California to prevent it from counting mail-in ballots from people the federal government has allegedly identified as “likely” noncitizens until their immigration status can be confirmed.

As my colleague Sam Levinereported on Thursday, the suit came two days after the DoJ made a specious demand to the state. On Tuesday, the department sent election officials in Los Angeles county a thumb drive with a handwritten password purporting to contain the names of non-citizens registered to vote. The department asked officials to confirm the citizenship of anyone on the list and set aside ballots from those whose status could not be confirmed. It gave the state 48 hours – an extremely narrow window – to take action. It did not provide details on how it came up with the names on the list. In its lawsuit, filed in federal court in the central district of California, the justice department said it had provided the state with more than 20,000 names of likely noncitizens.

A reminder that noncitizen voting is extremely rare and the effort to investigate noncitizen voting ahead of the midterm elections has only turned up a handful of cases so far. Today’s DoJ press release, incidentally, reaffirms this, with 28 an absolutely minuscule number compared with the 174 million people who were registered to vote in the 2024 presidential election.

In Sam’s piece last week, he also highlighted that the Trump administration’s methodology for identifying non-citizens has come under scrutiny. Earlier this year, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said there could be as many as 278,000 noncitizens on the rolls in four states, including more than 190,000 in California and about 16,000 in Nevada.

Officials at the DHS refused to share their methodology with Nevada election officials and later turned over just 185 names of people it had a strong belief were noncitizens. When Nevada officials investigated, they found every one of those people was a citizen.

As we mentioned earlier, Donald Trump is heading to Kansas today to open a seven-state campaign blitz through territory he carried in 2024, asdismalpolls and unexpectedly tight races in GOP strongholds stoke fears of sweeping Democratic gains in next month’s midterms.

With 15 days until the 3 November vote, Trump’s rally on the outskirts of Wichita aims to shore up the incumbent Republican senator RogerMarshall, who is locked in a dead heat with his Democratic opponent Adam Hamilton.
Trump won Kansas by 16 percentage points just two years ago, and the state has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932.
Yet analysts now rate it a “toss-up” and a key fundraising group for Republican senators has diverted money from North Carolina to defend a seat it once took for granted.

The University of Virginia’s Center for Politics told AFP it hesitated before moving deeply conservative Kansas into “toss-up” category – its most competitive – but was swayed by signs that a “full-on Republican rescue operation appears underway for Marshall”.
Control of Congress may hinge on such races, with Republicans holding slender majorities in both chambers, and Democrats needing a net gain of just four seats to capture the Senate.

Over the coming six days, Trump will follow Kansas with rallies in the Carolinas, Iowa, Florida, Georgia and Michigan. All seven states backed him in 2024, though his margins in Michigan, Georgia and North Carolina were narrow.
The schedule suggests the aim is less to win over undecided voters than to fire up loyal supporters, many of whom stay at home when he’s not on the ballot.
Two stops, North Carolina and Iowa, are damage control in GOP-held seats, and many national party officials have all but written off North Carolina.
Elsewhere the party is on the offensive, targeting a Democratic-held seat in Michigan, though it has struggled to make headway in Georgia.

Vice-President JD Vance is campaigning separately in NorthCarolina, Ohio and Nebraska. In North Carolina, sitting Republican representative, Jennifer Balkcom, is fending off a strong challenge from Democrat Jamie Ager.

At the White House today, Trump announced a new taskforce focused on women’s health. However, it’s worth remembering that under Joe Biden – first lady Jill Biden set up the first White House initiative of this kind in 2023.

Trump on Monday said that Susie Wiles, his chief of staff, would head up his administration’s taskforce. “Susie recently won her battle against a very tough opponent, breast cancer,” the president said. “It wasn’t easy. We went through it. We got her through it, and she got through it.”

And as another reminder, since Trump returned to office, his administration has gutted Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) funding for maternal health and fertility. The cuts to Medicaid through the One Big Beautiful Bill Act – Trump’s sweeping domestic policy legislation – will also affect pre- and perinatal care for pregnant people, according to experts.
Today’s new polling suggests Americans remain deeply pessimistic about the economy ahead of the midterms, with 75% rating conditions as either “not so good” or “poor”.
The findings also highlight the challenge facing Republicans in November: 37% of respondents said they trust Democrats more on the economy, compared with 28% who said they trust Republicans.

This comes as Trump continues his midterms campaign blitz this week. He’ll head to Kansas on Monday to stump on behalf of embattled GOP incumbent Senator Roger Marshall, before back-to-back events in North Carolina, South Carolina, Iowa, Florida, Georgia and Michigan.

Today’s announcement comes as billions of dollars have been scrapped from NIH research budgets. Almost 8,000 grants have been cancelled at the institute and the US National Science Foundation alone, and more than 1,000 NIH employees have been fired since Trump returned to office in 2025.
Earlier this year, my colleague Ed Pilkington, reported on the brain drain that was affecting the key agency that conducts biomedical and public health research.

A quick note that Donald Trump’s executive order signing at 11am ET will be to create a new Women’s Health Division at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and a White House Women’s Health taskforce, according to a White House official.
A reminder that Melania Trump, the first lady, will also be at the event.

The boss of a New York-based sticker company, whose staunch support for Donald Trump prompted him to record a Maga-themed rap album and call for an extension of Mount Rushmore to add the president’s face, is running for Congress.
Anthony Constantino, who began a brief pro boxing career at age 40, is the Republican candidate for GOP congresswoman Elise Stefanik’s seat in New York’s 21st district.

While Trump won the district by 21 points in 2024, and it has been represented by a Republican in the US House of Representatives since 2015, the party’s lead appears to have dwindled significantly as Constantino, 43, campaigns for voters to send him to Washington.

His lead in recent polls has fallen to single digits; one survey earlier this month put him four points behind. In September, the Cook Partisan Voting Index shifted the race from solid Republican to likely Republican. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee added the district to its Red to Blue program in early October.

“I’m running for Congress. I built a company with over 1,000 people. Not an easy thing to do,” Constantino said, referring to his company, Sticker Mule. “I went pro in boxing at the age of 40. Not an easy thing to do.”
Mike Tyson “decided to endorse me”, he added in an interview, claiming the former boxing world champion had only endorsed four candidates. “It’s not easy to get endorsed by Mike Tyson.”

Most political candidates lay out their agenda in lengthy publications, or campaign speeches. In December 2025, Constantino released a 20-track album – titled Thank You President Trump – which praised the president’s alleged golfing prowess and described how the world purportedly loves him. It took two weeks to complete, according to a press release.

“I just realize it’s good to be different, first of all,” Constantino said of the album. “Secondly, some people like listening to speeches. Other people like listening to music. Not everybody in this country wants to listen to political speeches.”

Also on Truth Social today, Donald Trump has repeated his baseless claims that the riots sweeping France – which initially began as protests against deteriorating school infrastructure and an overstretched education system – are due to mass migration.
“The migrants have taken over France. They must CLOSE THE BORDERS, FAST!” Trump wrote on social media.
A reminder that French authorities have not linked the riots to immigrants.

Over the weekend, hundreds of thousands demonstrated throughout the country. However, chaos erupted at a number of protests, which saw buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted and at least 2,400 people arrested.
French president Emmanuel Macron and the prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, have blamed the violence on “factious” ultra-leftwing groups.
Within the new polling from the Washington Post and ABC, 48% of respondents said they are financially worse off than when Trump returned to office in 2025.
According to the Post, that represents the highest percentage saying this about any president in this series of polls since 1986.

A majority of those surveyed – 67% – also said that Trump is not committed to protecting freedom of the press. This comes after a protracted battle to ban CNN, MS Now and Politico from the White House grounds. A federal judge has subsequently issued a preliminary injunction blocking the administration from enforcing the ban.
Meanwhile, 61 % people also said that Trump is not committed to free and fair elections, according to the poll.

articles.headline: New Pokémon Release Finally Lets You Play As Team Rocket
keyFacts: Team Rocket Evolved is a new fan-made Pokémon Emerald ROM hack that allows players to control a member of Team Rocket.
Players can steal Pokémon from other trainers and must conquer areas to access standard game features like Pokémon Centers.
Creators EricTurner3 and his wife are developing the project without AI and are currently accepting fan suggestions via their official subreddit.
body: Becoming the best that ever was? Boring. You've already played the plucky hero in Pokémon games — now, with a new upcoming game, you'll finally get to play as the villainous Team Rocket.

Such is the promise of Team Rocket Evolved, a new fan project for Pokémon Emerald that turns the monster-catching series on its head. You're still tasked with traveling the land and collecting gym badges, but the way you do it is totally different. In this version of the game, you can steal other trainers' Pokémon. If you're successful in pilfering the Pokémon, your opponent might just concede outright. Youngster Joey and his six Rattata never stood a chance.
Team Rocket Evolved gives the villains the starring role

Since you're terrorizing Hoenn, the locals will prove hostile in Team Rocket Evolved. Features like Pokémon Centers won't be accessible until after you take control of an area and beat its gym leader. There will be alternate ways of healing your Pokémon, but you should expect this alternate resource to be pricey and scarce. You can also call for backup from the larger organization — no one said the fight had to be fair!

The point of the game is to grow from being a lowly Team Rocket grunt to becoming a Team Rocket admin. In a refreshing change of pace, creator EricTurner3 said that he and his wife are not using AI to build the ROM hack. Despite the lack of AI, the development duo are still pulling out all the stops with their fan game. The finished, hand-crafted product is expected to offer every generation of Pokémon, including Mega Evolutions and Dynamax Evolutions. There are new types of trainers to encounter as well.

For the softies, Pokémon in this hack can still follow you around as they do in Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver. If the creators want to be realistic, the Pokémon you steal perhaps shouldn't be too friendly. A hack like this could be a great way to recontextualize instances where Pokémon don't obey the player's commands.
The Team Rocket Evolved project is still in development, and the creators are encouraging fans to send ideas or requests via the official subreddit.

articles.headline: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC
keyFacts: A Ukrainian presidential adviser said Ukrainians died due to incomplete US intelligence warnings about incoming Russian ballistic missile strikes.
US officials denied restricting intelligence sharing, while a Ukrainian adviser reported ongoing restrictions to Starlink services.
Ukraine is urgently seeking alternative communication systems to prepare for potential future problems with Starlink.
body: - Published
Ukrainians have died because Kyiv is still not receiving reliable US warnings of incoming Russian attacks, according to a key adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov told the BBC that lives had been lost because there had not been time to warn citizens about ballistic missile strikes, saying: "It's dangerous... I think it's really very bad... People [have] already died."
The adviser also said restrictions to Ukraine's use of the Starlink internet network were ongoing.
The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing with Ukraine.
Ukraine first reported an interruption to US intelligence sharing last week, as a row with the Trump administrations over its controversial deal to import Russian oil sent relations to new lows.
Despite the denials from Washington, many in Kyiv suspect the issues are not a coincidence.
On Monday morning, Zelensky wrote on social media: "Overnight two ballistic missile attacks were reported on the capital, one without warning, the second with only minimal time to take shelter."
Hours earlier, an interview the president did with NBC was published, in which he said intelligence sharing had been restored after a three-day pause.
"We are very thankful for this," he said. "Only [the] United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles."
But Beskrestnov told the BBC that American intelligence continued to be incomplete and inconsistent, and that the US had failed to provide a clear explanation for the issue.
"This looks very strange," he said. "Sometimes we receive this information before the attack, another time we [do] not."
He continued: "And for example, last night we received it, but... one minute before the attack."
However, he said other collaboration with US continues, adding: "Intelligence data keeps flowing, and the issue is solely with the air raid alert component."

Beskrestnov also said the US had given no clarity about who was responsible for the ongoing restrictions to the Starlink internet network and its military service Starshield, which Kyiv uses to provide connectivity for drones, helicopters and military communications.
Last week, Starshield restricted the speed at which mobile units could move while staying connected to the network to 100mph (160km/h).
This has limited Ukraine's ability to shoot down incoming drones or to launch mid-range drone attacks into Russian-occupied areas.

Starlink owner Elon Musk said last week that the US government ultimately controls access to Starshield, which was designed for the Pentagon, suggesting it may therefore be behind the restrictions. Trump has denied involvement.
Beskrestnov said he thought both issues occurring at the same time was "probably" a deliberate move to put pressure on Ukraine.
He told BBC News: "It's probably the United States trying to say [to] us, 'let's have the conversation, negotiation with Russia, you should find the compromise'."
Beskrestnov also said Ukraine had its own radar data to provide some limited warning of incoming attacks, but was urgently looking into using alternative communication systems.
He added: "Now we understand that something begins to happen with Starlink, and we're not sure what will be the next step.

"We understand that we should be prepared for some problems in future. And now we're thinking about an alternative for Starlink, not only for air defence, for communication between our forces, between our staff, for civilians also, because we don't know what we should expect in future regarding Starlink."
On Monday, when asked about intelligence sharing, Trump said: "We've given a lot to Ukraine. They've given us nothing."
Earlier, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had said there had not been a "pause" to intelligence sharing.
"I don't know where [Zelensky is] getting these things or why he's saying these things to the press," he told reporters on Monday.
Rubio said he could not comment on the incident, adding: "I know a few nights ago there was a software problem involving their early warning system."
The BBC has contacted Starlink for a response.
A White House official said there were no changes to intelligence sharing operations between the US and Ukraine.
The official spoke on background to discuss intelligence matters. Trump is focused on ending the war, the official said, and added that the US has provided more aid to Ukraine than any other country.

Russian attacks continued late on Monday, with Ukrainian officials saying at least six people were killed - including a toddler in her pram and an 11-year-old girl - in a drone strike near a park cafÃ© in the north-eastern Kharkiv region.
Zelensky described the attack in which another 14 people were injured as "absolute atrocity".

articles.headline: Trump calls on ‘somebody else’ to negotiate for Ukraine with Russia
keyFacts: Donald Trump recommended that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky nominate someone else to negotiate a peace deal with Russia.
